statement.before:
The wavelength at which the blackbody spectrum $B_\lambda(T)$ peaks is inversely proportional to the temperature:
$$\lambda_{\max} = \frac{b}{T},\qquad b = 2897.8\ \mu\text{m}\cdot\text{K}.$$
Earth at 288 K peaks near $10\ \mu$m, in the thermal infrared; the Sun at 5772 K near $0.50\ \mu$m, in the green. The constant depends on how the spectrum is measured: per unit frequency the peak lies at $\lambda T = 5099\ \mu$m·K, and per unit $\ln\lambda$ (equal energy per octave) at $3670\ \mu$m·K. All three move as $1/T$.

scope.before: Chosen Gaussian feedback centres/widths and equicorrelated errors, not published likelihoods or an inference from observed datasets. The process centre1.16 and width0.40 resemble the assessed process line; the other widths/centres are illustrative. A flat prior in feedback is not flat in ECS. All densities and intervals condition on positive restoring feedback. AR6 §7.5.5 explicitly discusses dependencies and expert judgement; Table 7.13 includes paleoclimate likely<4.5, verylikely>1.5 and extremelylikely<8K (the last is not mislabelled as a two-sided very-likely interval). [Primary assessment](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/downloads/report/IPCC_AR6_WGI_Chapter07.pdf).

scope.before: Fixed 300m deep, nonabsorbing, monodisperse liquid layer at chosen water path; $g=0.85$. The rational albedo curve is a chosen two-stream approximation, not Twomey's original numerical calculation. The independent angular Monte Carlo may differ systematically from that closure; it is an illustration, not a proof of the formula. A finite scattering limit records unresolved photons separately and bounds their possible reflection, instead of silently counting them as transmission. Global scaling uses 340 W/m² times a chosen affected fraction, neglecting atmospheric absorption, adjustments and spatial/diurnal weighting; it is not an ERF estimate. [Original Twomey1977](https://atmos.washington.edu/academics/classes/2008Q2/591A/Articles/twomey_i1520-0469-34-7-1149.pdf); AR6 Table7.8 is the source for the separately quoted assessed aerosol–cloud ERF.
